skill.name: get-available-resources
skill.description: Detect local CPU, GPU, memory, and disk resources for scientific computing tasks. The skill writes a resource report and recommends parallel, memory, GPU, and large-data strategies.
skill.summary: Detect local compute resources and plan scientific workloads.

content.value_statement: Scientific tasks fail when resource limits are unknown. This skill detects local CPU, GPU, memory, and disk capacity and recommends suitable computing strategies.
actual_capabilities: Detects CPU core counts, architecture, processor name, and available frequency data.
Reports RAM, swap, and disk capacity for the current working directory.
Checks NVIDIA, AMD, and Apple Silicon GPU availability through local system utilities.
Writes a local .claude_resources.json file with a timestamped resource snapshot.
Recommends parallel processing, memory, GPU, and large-data handling strategies.
limitations: Requires psutil, and GPU detection depends on vendor utilities being installed.
Reports a point-in-time snapshot, so memory and disk availability can change quickly.
Does not benchmark workloads or guarantee library compatibility on the detected hardware.
The generated resource file may expose machine details if committed or shared.

use_cases.title: Plan Large Data Analysis
use_cases.description: Check whether a dataset fits in memory before choosing pandas, Dask, Zarr, or streaming workflows.

use_cases.title: Choose Training Hardware
use_cases.description: Detect CUDA, ROCm, or Metal support before selecting a machine learning backend.

use_cases.title: Set Project Baselines
use_cases.description: Record local compute capacity before simulations, batch processing, or reproducibility planning.

prompt_templates.title: Check Before Analysis
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner resource check before a data task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use get-available-resources before analyzing this dataset. Summarize the detected limits and recommend a safe processing approach.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Parallel Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Run get-available-resources and choose a worker count for this batch job. Explain whether joblib, multiprocessing, or Dask fits best.

prompt_templates.title: Select Acceleration Backend
prompt_templates.prompt: Use get-available-resources to detect available GPUs. Recommend a PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX, or CPU backend for training.

prompt_templates.title: Design Resource-Aware Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow architecture for large scientific data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run get-available-resources, inspect the report, and design a pipeline for a dataset larger than memory with clear storage and compute choices.

output_examples.input: Run the skill before analyzing a 50 GB table dataset.
output_examples.output: The report shows available memory is below the dataset size. Use chunked loading with Dask or Zarr and avoid loading all rows at once.

output_examples.input: Check whether model training can use hardware acceleration.
output_examples.output: The report detects a supported GPU backend. Select the matching machine learning library and keep a CPU fallback for portability.

output_examples.input: Prepare to process thousands of files in parallel.
output_examples.output: The report recommends a worker count based on logical cores and reserves capacity for the operating system and other tasks.

best_practices: Run the skill before long or expensive computations so resource limits guide design choices.
Review the generated resource file before committing, publishing, or sharing project artifacts.
Re-run detection after changing machines, closing large applications, or adding new hardware.
anti_patterns: Do not assume a resource report is current after system load or disk usage changes.
Do not publish .claude_resources.json when machine details should remain private.
Do not treat recommendations as a substitute for benchmarking critical workloads.

faq.question: Does this skill send resource data over the network?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed files only collect local information and write a local JSON report.

faq.question: What file does the skill create?
faq.answer: By default it creates .claude_resources.json in the current working directory.

faq.question: Can I choose a different output path?
faq.answer: Yes. The detection script documents an output option for choosing another local path.

faq.question: Which platforms are supported?
faq.answer: The skill documents support for macOS, Linux, and Windows, with GPU checks that depend on platform tools.

faq.question: Does it install dependencies automatically?
faq.answer: No. The documentation says psutil is required and gives a separate install command.

faq.question: Can the recommendations replace performance testing?
faq.answer: No. They are planning guidance based on detected resources, not measured workload benchmarks.
